stem:
A barangay notice says: "The water supply will be cut off on Saturday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Please store enough water on Friday night."

Which of these is assumed by the notice?
choices: The water company is fixing a broken pipe on Saturday.
Residents are able to store water before the cut-off.
Every resident will run out of water on Saturday.
The water supply is cut off every Saturday.
answer: Residents are able to store water before the cut-off.
hints: An assumption is something the notice takes for granted but does not say. Ask what must be true for the advice "store enough water" to make sense.
Take one choice and imagine it is false. Start with the pipe: if no pipe is being fixed, does the notice still make sense?
Use the negation test on every choice: turn it into its opposite. If the notice still makes sense, that choice is not assumed. The assumed choice is the one whose opposite makes the advice pointless.

solution.methodName: Negation test: deny it, and see if the argument falls apart

steps.action: Find the notice's point: the water will be cut off, so residents should store water the night before.
steps.why: Before you look for an assumption, know what the speaker wants you to believe or do.

steps.action: Negate the pipe choice: "The company is not fixing a broken pipe." The notice still makes sense, because the cut-off could be for any reason.
steps.why: The notice never gives a reason for the cut-off, so it does not depend on any one reason.

steps.action: Negate the storing choice: "Residents are not able to store water before the cut-off." Now the advice to store water is pointless.
steps.why: This is the negation test. When the opposite of a choice makes the argument fall apart, the argument depends on that choice. That is the assumption.

steps.action: Negate the "every resident" choice: "Not every resident will run out of water." The notice still makes sense, since some residents will still need water.
steps.why: "Every" is too broad. The notice only needs some residents to need water, not all of them.

steps.action: Negate the last choice: "The supply is not cut off every Saturday." The notice is about this one Saturday, so it still makes sense.
The assumption is: Residents are able to store water before the cut-off.

trapNotes.The water company is fixing a broken pip: This is a likely reason, but the notice never gives one. Negate it: if no pipe is being fixed, the advice to store water still makes sense. So the notice does not depend on it.
trapNotes.Every resident will run out of water on: This is too broad. The notice only needs some residents to need water during the cut-off. If not everyone runs out, the advice still makes sense.
trapNotes.The water supply is cut off every Saturd: The notice is about this one Saturday only. Nothing says cut-offs happen every week, and the notice works either way.
